# Testament of Joseph — 11
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Cantabrigiensis) | **Section:** Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs

---

Joseph's testament is the longest and most personal. He is the one all the other brothers have been confessing about — the victim of jealousy, of conspiracy, of slander, of seduction. Now he speaks.

**1** He called his sons and his brothers together as he was dying. He said:

**2** Brothers, sons — hear Joseph, the one Israel loved.

**3** I have seen envy and death in my life. I did not go astray. I held to the truth of the LORD through all of it.

**4** My brothers hated me. God loved me. They wanted to kill me. God protected me. They threw me in a pit. God pulled me out. They sold me into slavery. God freed me. They took me captive. God reached down and held me up. They left me to starve. God fed me. They left me alone. God was with me. They left me sick. God visited me. They left me in prison. God showed me favor. They left me in chains. God released me. The Egyptians slander me. God defended me. My fellow slaves envied me. God exalted me.

**5** Potiphar — the captain of Pharaoh's guard — trusted me with his whole household. And then the struggle with his wife began.

**6** She came after me again and again. She threatened me with death. She had me punished and then called me back. She said: Give yourself to me and you will be lord of this house.

**7** I remembered my father's words. I went to my chamber. I wept. I prayed. I fasted — seven years of fasting. And God made me look well-nourished even through the fasting, because that is what God does for those who fast for his sake.

**8** When her husband was home she would drug his wine and try to get to me that way. When he was away, she threatened to accuse me. When she couldn't persuade me, she grabbed my coat.

**9** When brute force failed, she tried praise. She told me how pure I was, how holy. She promised to put in a good word with her husband. She said she would praise me before God. I was sick with grief at that — using holiness as a manipulation. I fled.

**10** She came to me sick, desperate, half-naked. She had planned how to beguile me. God guarded me from every device she deployed.

**11** Sons, look at what patience accomplishes. Look at what fasting and prayer accomplish.

**12** If you want the LORD to dwell with you — chase chastity and purity, hold them with patience, pray, fast, be humble. Because God loves chastity. And where God dwells, even if envy and slavery and slander find you — he will deliver you and exalt you, as he did for me. In deed, in word, in thought — he guards a person who walks this way.

**13** My brothers knew how my father favored me, and I never let it go to my head. I was young and I had the fear of God. I knew everything passes. I didn't use my father's love as a weapon against my brothers. I honored them. When they sold me, I didn't even tell the Ishmaelites who I was — I wouldn't use my father's name to shame them.

**14** Now sons: honor Levi and Judah. From them will come the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world — the one who saves all peoples and all Israel. His kingdom will never end. Mine will end the way a field-watcher's shelter disappears after the summer harvest is done.

**15** After I die, the Egyptians will oppress you. But God will bring you out and give you what he promised our fathers. When you go, take my bones with you. When those bones are carried up to the land, the LORD will be with you in light and Beliar will be left behind in darkness with Egypt.

**16** And take Asenath your mother and bury her near Rachel, your grandmother, at the Hippodrome.

**17** After he said these things, he stretched out his feet and fell into a beautiful and good sleep. All Israel mourned for him with a great mourning.

---
*End of Testament of Joseph*
